subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Vendors)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Johnson <sarah.johnson@acme.com>, Daniel Reyes <daniel.reyes@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs: Vendors)

Hi Sarah / Daniel,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier today — great to meet the team and walk through Acme's goals. Below is a concise recap and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned going into the bake-off.

Recap (high level)
- Primary pain points: unpredictable latency at scale (esp. bursty traffic), high per-token cost on current endpoints, and occasional hallucinations on multi-turn prompts used in search augmentation.
- Goals: a) bring P95 token latency under 350ms for common request sizes, b) reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by >=25%, and c) demonstrate parity or improvement on Acme's NLU accuracy tests (intent classification + entity extraction).
- Decision criteria: latency (P50/P95), total cost (1M-token baseline), quality (benchmarked on your eval prompts), security/compliance posture (SOC2 + data retention options), and operational maturity (SLOs, tracing, rollout tools).

Open questions we captured
- Which exact model sizes (and sequence lengths) are you planning to include in the bake-off?
- Any data residency constraints for test runs or telemetry we should be aware of?
- Do you have a preferred baseline vendor set we should expect to compete against (we heard Vendor A and Vendor B mentioned)?

Proposed bake-off tests (what Redwood will run)
1) Latency profile: run 10k requests across typical payload sizes to report P50/P95/P99 and cold vs warm (with KV/prefix caching).
2) Cost simulation: estimate per-1M token cost across our recommended quantization and batching configurations.
3) Quality evals: run your intent/entity prompt set and return accuracy/precision/recall and failure examples.
4) Stress and failure modes: simulate burst concurrency to validate graceful degradation and fallbacks.

Attachments: I attached our bake-off checklist and a short performance report from a similar customer to give the team context.

Next steps / timeline
- We propose a 2-week run window: start Mon Jun 21, complete by Fri Jul 2.
- Action items: (a) Acme to share sample eval prompts + a small dataset (S3 link preferred), (b) Redwood SE (Michael) to confirm exact test harness and schedule a 30–45 min kickoff, (c) procurement/security to flag any additional docs needed (SOC2, encryption, data retention).

Michael — can you own the test scaffolding and proposed run commands? Vivek — can you compile our SOC2 + compliance summary to share with Acme?

Sarah / Daniel — are you good with the proposed window and tests, or should we shift timing?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0196

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-checklist.xlsx, redwood-performance-report.pdf

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (Redwood vs. Vendors)

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. This aligns with our internal notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Model sizes: we'll include the "medium" and "large" production profiles (up to 8k tokens for some longer context experiments).
2) Priority: latency and accuracy are weighted most heavily; cost is important but secondary to not regressing on intent accuracy.
3) Security/compliance: procurement will need SOC2 Type II and our standard DPA before any run that uses customer data. Can you include Vivek's compliance summary as soon as possible?

I'm looping in Daniel (CTO) — he'll want to see the test plan. Procurement (procurement@acme.com) will follow up on DPA details if needed.

We are OK with the Jun 21 start date, but procurement paperwork may add a few days — we'll keep you posted.

Thanks,
Sarah Johnson
Product Lead, Search
Acme Corp

Hi Sarah / team,

Thanks — quick technical follow-up with how we'll operationalize the tests and what we need from you.

Test harness overview
- We'll run an automated harness that: issues requests at configured QPS, measures P50/P95/P99 latency, collects token counts, and records model outputs for the quality eval suite. Results will be pushed to a temporary S3 bucket (read-only for Acme).
- For cold vs warm measurements we'll include a cache warm-up phase and report both pre/post warm-up metrics.

What we need from Acme
- Sample prompts: a CSV with one prompt per line (and expected labels for the eval).
- Representative concurrency profile: expected QPS and typical payload sizes.
- A redacted sample of the 8k-token longer contexts (if possible) — can be synthetic if regulatory concerns exist.

Proposed schedule
- Kickoff call (30 min) to align on schedule and S3 access: Tue Jun 22 at 10:00am PT — please confirm.
- Run window: Jun 23–Jun 30 (adjustable if procurement delays).

Security note: We will only store run artifacts in an Acme-controlled S3 path and delete artifacts on completion unless you instruct otherwise. We'll provide a short compliance packet and the SOC2 summary (Vivek to attach).

I'll prepare the harness repo and share the run commands in a follow-up.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
